question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y={(2x-3)}^{7}{({x}^{3}+5)}^{4}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(2x-3)}^{7}{({x}^{3}+5)}^{4}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(2x-3)}^{7})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({({x}^{3}+5)}^{4}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =7\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x-3)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x-3)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}+5)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =7\cdot \frac{2}{2x-3}+4\cdot \frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+5} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =7\cdot \frac{2}{2x-3}+4\cdot \frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(7\cdot \frac{2}{2x-3}+4\cdot \frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+5})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={(2x-3)}^{7}{({x}^{3}+5)}^{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={(2x-3)}^{7}{({x}^{3}+5)}^{4}(7\cdot \frac{2}{2x-3}+4\cdot \frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}+5}) \\  & ={(2x-3)}^{6}{({x}^{3}+5)}^{3}[14({x}^{3}+5)+12{x}^{2}(2x-3)] \\  & ={(2x-3)}^{6}{({x}^{3}+5)}^{3}(38{x}^{3}-36{x}^{2}+70)\end{aligned}
$$
